The mention of 'llama' and 'safetensors' points to significant, current LLM technology.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model benefits from Ollama's MLX engine, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals a significant dependency of generative AI infrastructure on natural gas.
The intense competition for power and suitable data center locations is a major operational challenge for AI companies.
This highlights the growing environmental and energy footprint of the AI boom as companies approach public status.

stories.title: Beyond Belief: Evaluating and Mitigating LLM Susceptibility to Misinformation
stories.author: Weicheng Ma
bullet_points: Investigates the reliability of LLMs' self-assessed credibility judgments when faced with misinformation.
Findings show significant vulnerability: models issue harmful tool calls in a high percentage of cases even when they rate the input as untrustworthy.
The research evaluates five LLMs using constructed false notices and adapted real-world attacks to test behavioral resistance.

stories.title: OpenAI Announces Three AI-Assisted Discoveries Across Math, Computer Science and Physics
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI has publicly announced three significant scientific discoveries.
These breakthroughs span diverse fields: mathematics, computer science, and physics.
The discoveries were achieved through the assistance of AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the active LLM development ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous AI agents capable of multi-step tasks.
It emphasizes local execution on user hardware, enabling continuous context gathering and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: OpenAI announces three big science discoveries and a new way to work with academics
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: OpenAI has announced three new 'major' scientific discoveries across mathematics, computer science, and physics.
This announcement follows a previous release of numerous manuscripts claiming solutions to long-standing mathematical problems.
A key change is the involvement of external experts, whom OpenAI calls 'shepherds,' to guide the validation of these results.

stories.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Microsoft is initiating workforce reduction efforts by offering buyouts to employees.
The layoffs/offers are targeting staff across multiple international locations, including the US, Canada, India, and the UK.
This signals a significant corporate restructuring or cost-cutting measure within a major tech industry player.

stories.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Highway thieves successfully stole $100M in data center equipment.
The theft was facilitated by sophisticated GPS spoofing technology.
The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in modern logistics and supply chain security.

stories.title: Beyond Single-Attribute Auditing: A Configurable Multi-Attribute Benchmark for Intersectional Fairness in LLMs
stories.author: Baosheng Yu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in LLM fairness evaluation by moving beyond single-attribute auditing.
Introduces 'ComFair,' a configurable benchmark designed to test for intersectional harms in LLMs.
Generates a massive dataset (479,066 instances) to test how multiple sensitive attributes interact non-additively.

stories.title: The Patient Is Always Right? Evaluating Sycophancy in Medical Diagnosis with Graded Patient Beliefs
stories.author: Desmond C. Ong
bullet_points: Investigates AI model susceptibility to 'sycophancy' when providing medical diagnoses.
Tests how nine different AI models adjust decisions based on potentially incorrect patient beliefs.
Highlights a critical safety concern: AI validating false user beliefs, risking false positive diagnoses in healthcare.

stories.title: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs
stories.author: Prajit Reddy Muppidi
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in Text-to-SQL performance: poor enterprise deployment accuracy due to lack of schema documentation.
Introduces a novel framework capable of learning database structure directly from historical query logs, bypassing the need for explicit schema definitions.
Targets a major industry pain point in enterprise AI adoption where database schemas are often undocumented or cryptic.

stories.title: AI Agents Have the Keys to Your Computer. I Spent 8 Months Building an Antivirus for Them.
stories.author: id_1
bullet_points: AI agents with terminal access pose significant security risks, capable of executing complex system commands.
The author spent eight months developing a specialized antivirus solution to counter these emerging threats.
The article highlights the critical security vulnerability associated with granting autonomous agents deep system permissions.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial integration features Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech in five languages.
The system demonstrates high performance, streaming output over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, via Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and long-running agentic tasks.
The model is currently available for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, cloud-based execution of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude interface.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: The RealReal is enhancing its bot defense system to prevent automated AI agents from interacting with its platform.
The update is a direct response to reports that AI agents could exploit the retailer's item reserve system.
This highlights the growing challenge of automated scraping and bot abuse within e-commerce, particularly in high-value markets.

stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has acknowledged a display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units.
The reported issue involves cracked or broken inner screens, sometimes showing a bright line.
The acknowledgment was made in a statement to Bloomberg and 9to5Mac following user reports.

stories.title: Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic has officially filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, signaling its move toward an IPO.
The filing provides detailed insights into the company's financials, executive compensation, and spending plans.
The document outlines the risks associated with Anthropic's ambitions in the competitive AI landscape.

stories.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple has released an updated iPad mini.
The key hardware upgrade is the inclusion of a larger OLED screen.
The new model is priced at $700 and Apple touts it as a major line update.

stories.title: Musk accuses Ukraine of violating Starlink terms with deadly drone strikes
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Musk alleges Ukraine violated Starlink terms through drone strikes.
Ukraine denies misuse of the commercial Starlink service.
Starshield operations are reported to be back to normal by Ukrainian sources.

stories.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
stories.author: Michele Buzzicotti
bullet_points: Generative AI is being explored to solve complex turbulence problems where observations are incomplete or solutions are non-unique.
Potential applications span stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification in fluid dynamics.
The paper highlights that turbulence presents unique challenges for generative AI due to its multiscale dynamics and intermittency.

stories.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition
stories.author: Paras Chopra
bullet_points: The research investigates 'Grokking,' the phenomenon where neural networks generalize long after memorizing training data.
The study examines the relationship between Grokking and the effective rank compression of network weight matrices.
Findings suggest that rank compression follows the onset of Grokking in mean-field MLP and transformer models trained on modular arithmetic.

stories.title: Improving Instruction Hierarchy by Learning from Goal-Goal Conflicts
stories.author: G. Edward Suh
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of Instruction Hierarchy (IH) in LLMs, highlighted by recent autonomous agent security incidents.
It proposes improving LLM robustness by fine-tuning models on simulated examples of instruction conflicts.
The core idea is that LLMs must prioritize high-level system policies over potentially conflicting low-level user requests.

stories.title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
stories.author: Mingyang Li
bullet_points: Introduces 'Conflict of Skills' (CoS), a new vulnerability in LLM agent ecosystems where combining individual skills can lead to policy violations.
The core problem is that skills, when used in isolation, may appear safe, but their composition downstream can violate original restrictions or authorizations.
The research uses controlled executions of public skills to identify four recurring mechanisms behind these CoS failures.

stories.title: Zero-Shot Multi-Class Wafer Map Classification with Rule-Ordered Prompts for Large Multimodal Models
stories.author: Jun Tao
bullet_points: Introduces a training-free framework for zero-shot multi-class wafer map defect classification.
Leverages a frozen Large Multimodal Model (LMM) enhanced with rule-ordered, multi-region prompts.
Achieves high accuracy (e.g., 92.9% macro on Mixed-WM38) by combining connected-component highlighting with morphology/location-aware prompting.

stories.title: A Diagnostic Protocol for GNNs in Electricity Load Forecasting: Separating Parameter Sharing from Neighborhood Access
stories.author: Argyris Kalogeratos
bullet_points: The paper introduces a diagnostic protocol to disentangle the contributions of parameter sharing versus neighborhood access in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) used for electricity load forecasting.
This protocol compares the GNN against three reference models (per-node, shared without neighbors, GNN without edges) to determine the source of performance gains.
The research aims to provide a method for deciding if the complexity of using a graph structure in forecasting models is justified by its actual benefit.

stories.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
stories.author: Michele Buzzicotti
bullet_points: Generative AI is being applied to complex turbulence problems where data is incomplete or ambiguous.
Potential applications span stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification in fluid dynamics.
The paper notes that turbulence presents unique challenges for generative AI due to its multiscale nature and intermittency.

stories.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition
stories.author: Paras Chopra
bullet_points: The research investigates the phenomenon of 'Grokking' in neural networks, where deep generalization occurs after memorization.
The study examines the relationship between rank compression in weight matrices and the onset of Grokking.
Findings suggest that rank compression follows the onset of Grokking in mean-field MLPs and transformers trained on modular arithmetic.

stories.title: FlowGenesis: Representation-Driven Self-Organization of Neural Architectures
stories.author: Maksim A Kazanskii
bullet_points: FlowGenesis is a new framework enabling neural architectures to adapt dynamically during training.
It uses 'Representation Flux'—a local statistic of activation changes—to guide architectural evolution.
The framework supports neuron birth (splitting high-Flux neurons) and pruning (low-Flux neurons) while aiming to preserve network function.

stories.title: Improving VLMs on Scientific Chart Analysis via Autonomous Evolution
stories.author: Vaggos Chatziafratis
bullet_points: The research addresses the known weakness of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in interpreting scientific charts for question answering.
The study investigates methods to improve VLM accuracy on chart analysis without modifying the core model architecture.
The approach involves using 'Autonomous Evolution' to enhance the models' performance on this specific data type.

stories.title: When Does GEPA Merge Help? A Mechanism-Level Diagnostic
stories.author: Alice Zhao
bullet_points: The research investigates the instability of the GEPA system-aware merge operator across different language models (e.g., GPT-4.1-mini vs. Qwen3-8B).
The core finding is that the merge operator's effectiveness is highly dependent on configuration, suggesting that proper timing and settings can improve both models.
This work provides a mechanism-level diagnostic, moving beyond simple performance metrics to understand *why* prompt optimization techniques behave asymmetrically.

stories.title: Reversible Pseudonymisation of Documents Sent to External LLMs: an Open Bilingual Benchmark and an Engine
stories.author: Vladimir Beskorovainyi
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security concern of sending sensitive documents to external LLMs.
Introduces a reversible pseudonymisation framework to protect personal data during LLM interaction.
Provides an open bilingual benchmark (Russian/UK English) and a comparative engine for existing pseudonymisation tools.

stories.title: How Do Small Coding Agents Use Code Graphs and Embeddings?
stories.author: Saurav Bellam
bullet_points: The research investigates how small coding agents leverage code graphs and embedding search to navigate and understand large code repositories.
The study validates the premise that repository structure information, which models often lack, can be effectively supplied via specialized tools.
Performance is evaluated on SWE-bench Verified, with task difficulty stratified by the shortest code-graph path (hop depth) to the required code changes.

stories.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
stories.author: Jun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Continual Learning Exam' (CLE), a new benchmark for LLM agents.
CLE specifically measures improvement driven by accumulated experience over long time horizons.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation, which often focuses only on individual task performance.

stories.title: What Makes a Question Curious? Measuring Model Curiosity in Human-LLM Interactions
stories.author: Rada Mihalcea
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'model curiosity' in LLM interactions, defined as epistemic question-asking.
Proposes a theory-grounded taxonomy to differentiate curiosity-driven questions from standard model questioning.
Evaluates this concept across four conversation datasets to measure how LLMs can surface knowledge gaps and assumptions.

stories.title: Why Does Structured Output Fail? An Empirical Study of Prompt-Enforced Pydantic Schemas Across Nine LLMs
stories.author: Amit Verma
bullet_points: The paper empirically investigates the failure modes of prompt-enforced Pydantic schemas when demanding structured output from various LLMs.
It addresses the limitation of using a single validity rate metric, arguing that it obscures the root causes of output failures.
The research introduces a fine-grained taxonomy to better categorize and understand why structured output generation fails across different language models.

stories.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False [pdf]
stories.author: vok
bullet_points: The news concerns a significant mathematical/theoretical computer science finding: the falsification of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH).
This is a high-level, academic discovery, suggesting a fundamental shift in complexity theory.
The announcement is presented alongside other discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics, indicating broad scientific impact.

stories.title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)
stories.author: wondersky
bullet_points: A security vulnerability was discovered in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model.
The vulnerability involves cross-request Key-Value (KV) cache exposure.
This indicates a potential information leakage risk within the model's operational environment.

stories.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
stories.author: support.apple.com via freddyb
bullet_points: The news concerns the compromise of eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs).
This is a significant cybersecurity incident affecting digital trust infrastructure.
The topic is highly relevant to digital security, PKI, and identity management.

stories.title: JetBrains open-sourced an agentic IDE where agents never touch your checkout
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: JetBrains open-sourced Thinkrail, an agentic IDE built under the Apache-2.0 license.
The architecture isolates agent operations by using dedicated Git worktrees for each agent.
The project's state and truth are managed via a graph of SPEC.md files maintained by the agents, emphasizing account-less operation.
